source_text: Quia de vobis multitudini mentiti fuerimus, et quod Caelestianorum vel Pelagianorum nomine homines terreamus, et quod terrore ab hominibus extorqueamus assensum Tamquam non invenirem quid facerem, quo confugerem, si iudicum premerer potestate, si in medio eruditorum consisterem tecum, si verae
pass_a_gloss: Because about/from to-you to-the-crowd having-lied fuerimus, and that/which Caelestianorum or Pelagianorum by-name human-beings we-frighten, and that/which by-terror from hominibus we-extort agreement Tamquam not invenirem what facerem, whither confugerem, if of-judges i-were-pressed by-power, if in medio of-the-learned i-stood tecum, if verae.
pass_b_english: [He would not] find anything to do or anywhere to turn, if pressed by the judges’ authority, if standing with me among learned people, if the trumpet of true reason and the weapons of the listeners standing around rang out.
[They] have lied to the crowd about us; they frighten people with the names “Caelestians” or “Pelagians,” and force agreement from people through fear.
All judges ought to be free from hatred, friendship, hostility, and anger.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
